record.title: A preprint defines a Fisher leverage measure for comparing language-model weight updates
record.summary: An October 27 arXiv preprint introduces leverage, the Fisher quadratic form of a weight update divided by the same form for a random direction of equal size at the same checkpoint. Across released Olmo-3, Tülu-3, Zephyr and OLMo-2 checkpoints, the author reports leverage near 1 for two pretraining windows on a 51,167-token mixed corpus, about 5 for SFT, hundreds to low thousands for RL-Zero/RLVR, and values from hundreds to tens of thousands for DPO. Controlled training and one released OLMo-2 DPO recipe rerun support some of the reported contrasts. The paper also reports that a sign-structure term predicts damage from random delta sparsification in tested cases. These are author-reported research results. The metric measures local next-token distribution change, not task capability; results are bounded by the corpora and training regimes studied, and no independent reproduction was performed here.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The author defines leverage as an update direction’s Fisher quadratic form divided by the mean form for random directions of the same size at the same checkpoint, using an exact forward-mode Jacobian-vector product rather than a finite-difference approximation. It measures local next-token-distribution change per weight displacement, not task capability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across released checkpoints, the paper reports leverage near 1 for two Olmo-3 pretraining windows on a 51,167-token four-domain corpus, about 5 for SFT, roughly 388–1,508 for RL-Zero/RLVR, and roughly 378–22,570 for DPO. These are author-computed values on selected models, deltas and corpora.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In controlled experiments, the author reports that update leverage falls as SFT or DPO trajectories move at 0.5B and 7B, and that two reruns of one released OLMo-2-1B DPO recipe match its released displacement and leverage within 1% and 4%, respectively. Seed counts are two or three in many comparisons; the 7B controlled arms have one seed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For tested released deltas where predicted damage was below about 0.5, the paper reports that its sign-flip null predicted random drop-and-rescale sparsification damage within a factor of 2.1. The relation breaks down when predicted damage is large; the study tested six deltas and three keep rates.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish that leverage measures task capability, that higher leverage causes better downstream performance, that local rankings persist on longer or task-specific data, or that its conclusions generalize across training systems and model families. The stated extrapolation tests are inconclusive.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported exact Fisher measurements, null draws and checkpoint comparisons have not been independently reproduced in this review; the paper says it will release code and corpora.
The headline measure is averaged over a 51,167-token four-domain corpus and a small number of released deltas; it is not established on longer or task-specific evaluation data.
The paper’s preregistered extrapolation predictions perform inconclusively on small numbers of scorable GSM8K and MATH-500 deltas.

brief.importance_rationale: If robust across models and evaluation regimes, an update-to-random Fisher ratio could help characterize how fine-tuning changes model outputs and how safely weight deltas can be sparsified. The reported measure is local and corpus-specific, so its implications for task performance and training decisions are not established.
limitations: All quantitative findings are author-reported and were not independently reproduced here.
The headline corpus has 51,167 tokens across four domains; transfer to longer or task-specific corpora is not established.
Many controlled comparisons use two or three seeds; 7B controlled arms use one seed, and the OLMo-2 reproduction covers one released DPO stage.
Leverage is local Fisher curvature of next-token distributions and does not directly measure task capability or usefulness.
The paper reports inconclusive extrapolation tests.
bf16 storage can zero coordinates and distort some reported alignment measures.
brief.summary: An October 27 arXiv preprint introduces leverage, the Fisher quadratic form of a weight update divided by the same form for a random direction of equal size at the same checkpoint. Across released Olmo-3, Tülu-3, Zephyr and OLMo-2 checkpoints, the author reports leverage near 1 for two pretraining windows on a 51,167-token mixed corpus, about 5 for SFT, hundreds to low thousands for RL-Zero/RLVR, and values from hundreds to tens of thousands for DPO. Controlled training and one released OLMo-2 DPO recipe rerun support some of the reported contrasts. The paper also reports that a sign-structure term predicts damage from random delta sparsification in tested cases. These are author-reported research results. The metric measures local next-token distribution change, not task capability; results are bounded by the corpora and training regimes studied, and no independent reproduction was performed here.

technical.claimed_result: A Fisher-based matched-random ratio separates selected released training-stage deltas by several orders of magnitude on the author’s evaluation corpora. The paper reports controlled trajectory and one-recipe reproduction results, plus a bounded sparsification-damage relation.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 HTML paper, method, result tables, limitations and selected appendices were inspected. No code or corpus was run and no independent reproduction was conducted.
technical.mechanism: The exact measure is a second-order Fisher quadratic for the next-token distribution under fixed text, normalized by equal-size random weight directions at the same anchor. Sign-flip and per-tensor profile nulls separate cross-coordinate sign structure from magnitude alignment.
technical.regime: Released Olmo-3-7B, Tülu-3-8B, Zephyr-7B and OLMo-2 checkpoints; controlled Qwen2.5 runs at 0.5B and 7B; an OLMo-2-1B DPO rerun. The headline mixed corpus contains 51,167 tokens across web, chat, math and code. Most reported controlled comparisons use two or three seeds.
technical.reproducibility: The author reports a recipe rerun that matched one released DPO delta within 1% in displacement and 4% in leverage. The author states that code and corpora will be released. This review did not independently inspect or execute the artifacts.
technical.strongest_baseline: At the author’s 51,167-token mixed corpus, two Olmo-3 pretraining windows had reported leverage 0.78 and 0.95 against an isotropic random-direction null of 1; selected post-training deltas had much higher reported values. The paper’s evaluation is local output-distribution curvature, not task performance.

brief.title: A preprint defines a Fisher leverage measure for comparing language-model weight updates
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced and linked to task-level outcomes, a matched-random Fisher measure could help compare how training stages alter model outputs and estimate when weight-delta sparsification will cause damage. The paper does not establish that higher leverage means better capability or that its conclusions generalize to other models, tasks or training pipelines.
